purpose: Open design question with real options to weigh, BEFORE building. Cross-vendor on purpose: a second opinion from the same family that wrote the code is one instrument twice. #1355 tried making this read-shaped (write_files: false, the review/fact-check/patch shape) but reverted it: advise's tier defaults to agy, which was not outbox-write-capable, and tools/baton-agy-loop/dispatch.py's grant_refusal() refused a withheld-write role on a non-outbox-capable adapter outright by design rather than auto-granting the audited write the C# engine's RoleDispatch now does. #1759 retired dispatch.py; #1386 redid the narrowing under the real production sequence (RoleDispatch.ToBinding -> WorktreeWorkspaces.Provision -> WorkerBindingResolver.Resolve) where #901's audited-write widening un-refuses a withheld-write role once a worktree is provisioned, so no tier move is needed either. #1861 then moved the standard tier off agy for measured reasons (docs/dispatch.md's tier paragraph), so an unmodified advise dispatch now runs its withheld write ENFORCED against the caller's directory rather than audited in a fresh worktree; the agy path above remains what --adapter agy takes. Which vendor the standard tier names today is WorkerTiers.json's to say, not this sentence's -- it has moved once since (#1863) and the conclusion above holds for any outbox-write-capable vendor it names.

outputs.name: advice.md
outputs.instruction: Write your recommendation -- the options you weighed and your reasoning -- to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/advice.md.

purpose: A bounded change with the approach already decided. Exercises the write path -- and, under --adapter agy (the tier's default until #1861 moved it onto claude), agy's skip-permissions translation -- which is the half of AER that review-only dispatches never touch. Its 40 minutes is NOT the #588 path -- every template's timeout exercises that equally -- so do not reach for the skip-permissions grant expecting it to buy that. #1355 kept network_access true here: PermissionGrant.CategoriesDefeatedByTheShell/WorkerBindingResolver refuse RunShellCommands without NetworkAccess outright for EVERY grant-consuming adapter, claude included, not agy alone (--adapter claude is not an escape hatch) -- and agy's own AgyWorkerAdapter.TryTranslatePermissionGrant refuses the same combination a second time at the vendor-translation layer, since --dangerously-skip-permissions grants both or neither. Defaulting network off here would make every unmodified dispatch of this role throw. See #1387 for the follow-up this leaves open.

outputs.name: changes.md
outputs.instruction: Write a summary of the changes you made -- which files, and what and why -- to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/changes.md. This is a floor and a handoff, not proof the change is correct; a following review verifies that against the diff.

purpose: A conductor-selected measurement with executable tools and an artifact-only completion contract. It may create and clean up isolated local fixtures. Its grant retains positional deny patterns for direct commit, push, PR-mutation and issue-mutation spellings as defense in depth, but the unscoped shell matcher is not a categorical shell sandbox and cannot cover alternate CLI spellings; the role instruction and operator policy remain the broader no-shipping boundary. The role is selected before launch and persisted through the ordinary queue and binding records; worker prose and report content cannot turn an implement lane into this contract. A non-empty report is the whole delivered result, so no workspace gate, branch push or PR is required. The token, tool-step and timeout defaults reuse implement's existing ceilings rather than inventing measurement calibration; a bounded brief may override them downward through the queue's existing flags.

outputs.name: report.md
outputs.instruction: Write the measurement report -- method, evidence, validation performed, results, uncertainty, and any reproducible local artifact paths -- to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/report.md. Do not commit, push, open or edit a PR, or mutate an issue. Direct spellings are covered by positional deny patterns, but those patterns are not a categorical shell sandbox; alternate CLI spellings remain prohibited by this role instruction and operator policy. The report must contain non-whitespace content or the declared output contract fails.

purpose: Adversarial review of CLAIMS -- a decision record, a measured finding, anything whose rationale asserts something. The default for any PR touching src/ or making a claim in docs/. #1456 (spec/baton.md SS9) grants read-only git/gh so scope no longer has to be reconstructed from grep and .git ref reads: the allowlist above is claude's real, measured ceiling (docs/vendor-capabilities.md's 'canonical ceiling' -- --allowedTools patterns plus a --disallowedTools deny-subset, both enforced with precedence, not mere pre-approval) rather than a wider categorical run_shell_commands. gh api is deliberately excluded -- its method is a runtime flag/field this glob matcher cannot bind to GET-only, so admitting it would be an unenforced hole, not a scoped one. This reverses #1355's flat shell refusal for review specifically because that decision's own reasoning was agy's incoherence (no scoped-shell-without-network grant exists there); #1387 closed that gap -- AgyWorkerAdapter.TryTranslatePermissionGrant now defers a pattern-scoped shell grant like this one to AER's own PreToolUse hook instead of refusing it outright, so --adapter agy is a supported override here too. What was measured is the run_command channel narrowing this exact allow/deny list correctly, on six probed commands (docs/vendor-doc-audit.md) -- not the subagent/manage_task tools (denied outright, #1387 review F1), not the read tools' absent path bound (F2), and not the allow/deny lists' own prefix-collision defects (git diff*/git grep*/git merge-base*, #1679), so 'measured end to end' overstates the population; see spec/baton.md SS9 for the qualified claim. #1679 fixed those collisions by matching trailing-* patterns on word boundaries, and its review (#1683) then showed a positional deny cannot bound an OPTION at all: git grep is gone from the allowlist (the harness's own Grep tool covers a reviewer's need, and -O/--open-files-in-pager spawns an arbitrary pager through clustering, reordering or abbreviation that no anchored pattern catches), and denied_shell_option_tokens closes --output, the arbitrary file write git log/show/diff admitted under this role's own shell_commands_are_read_only assertion. The tier still defaults to claude (WorkerTiers.json's frontier entry) -- this only means an operator override no longer hits PermissionGrantUnsupportedException.

outputs.name: report.md
outputs.instruction: Write your prose review -- each finding with file:line evidence -- to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/report.md.

outputs.name: verdict.json
outputs.instruction: Also write your findings as a ReviewVerdict JSON to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/verdict.json (the machine-checked structured form of the same review). decision is one of approve/block -- your own call on whether the reviewed change is ready, never derived from the findings; always write it, since a verdict without it stops the work for a person rather than carrying the round. severity is one of high/medium/low; status is one of confirmed/refuted/unverified; unlisted fields are ignored; findings may be an empty array. Example: {"reviewedRef":"<branch, commit, or PR>","decision":"block","summary":"<optional overall assessment>","findings":[{"claim":"<one-line finding>","severity":"high","status":"confirmed","anchor":{"file":"path/to/file","line":1},"detail":"<evidence, reproduction, reasoning>"}]}

purpose: Consolidate one issue against the code: read its thread and merged PRs, check each claim against the tree, and write the current-state block a person rewrites the issue body from (#2043). This exists because the conductor dispatched three such reads through its host's own sub-agent tool rather than baton lanes -- the dogfood rule broken by the person building the tool -- and the two measured costs were the GRANT (a thread-plus-PRs-plus-code read wants `gh issue view --comments`, `gh pr diff --stat` and file reads; every refused `cd`/`cat`/pipe/`git grep` habit cost a refused step and a rephrase) and the OUTPUT SHAPE (this produces a text block for the operator, never a PR). Both are answered by declaring them once here rather than re-negotiated per dispatch. Grant: `review`'s measured ceiling narrowed, never widened -- the allowlist is a strict SUBSET of review's (no `git status`/`rev-parse`/`merge-base`/`branch --list`/`gh pr checks`, none of which a consolidation reads), the deny list and `--output` option deny are review's verbatim, and `WorkerRoleCatalogTests` pins both relations so a future widening here is loud instead of invisible; review's own purpose field is where that ceiling's measurement lives, not restated. Tier is `frontier` on docs/agents/developing-baton.md's membership test: the `stale` section is 'notice a thread claim the code now contradicts', which is noticing something absent from the list it was handed, so a weaker model could plausibly reach the opposite conclusion for a reason unrelated to the issue. Writes nothing and pushes nothing -- `delivers_branch` and `verifies_workspace` both stay false, and stage-less `baton queue add --role consolidate` items are never advanced by `WorkItemLifecycle`, so nothing on the settle path ever asks this lane for a PR. Both arrest triggers are set rather than left null, because a frontier role reading a long thread and several PR diffs unwatched is the operator's money: the token budget is `review`'s figure unchanged (same tier, same read shape, same 25-minute wall clock), and the tool-step cap is above review's 100 because this lane reads N PRs AND re-checks each claim against the tree where a review reads one diff. 150 is a reasoned starting ceiling, not a measurement -- revisit it against the first live lanes the way #1686 revisited review's.

outputs.name: consolidation.md
outputs.instruction: Write the consolidated current-state block to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/consolidation.md, under exactly these four headings, in this order: '## Shipped, verified in code' (only what you confirmed against the tree, each line carrying the file:line that proves it), '## Remains' (what the issue still asks for that no code does yet), '## Stale' (what the thread asserts that the code now contradicts, with the evidence that contradicts it), '## Next slice' (the smallest shippable next step). Read the thread with `gh issue view <n> --comments` and each merged PR with `gh pr view <n>` and `gh pr diff <n> --stat`; read the tree with your harness's own file-read and search tools rather than the shell -- `cd`, `cat`, `head`, pipes and `git grep` are not in this role's grant (#1683 ruled the harness's own search tool covers this need), so every attempt costs you a refused step. The file must not be empty: its schema is checked, so a lane that writes nothing fails rather than settling.

purpose: Proposes code modifications as an applyable unified diff without mutating its workspace directly (withheld writes run enforced on claude, and audited-not-enforced on agy per #659).

outputs.name: patch.diff
outputs.instruction: Write your proposed changes as a unified diff against your workspace to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/patch.diff. If you propose no changes, write an empty file.

purpose: 'Confirm these specific facts against the repo.' Handed an exhaustive list, so the list determines the work and a cheap model runs it. NOT for anything where noticing something absent from the list is the point.

outputs.name: findings.md
outputs.instruction: Write your findings -- each claim from the list and whether it holds, with evidence -- to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/findings.md.

purpose: After an implementer commits: run the named mechanical checkers and make them green without changing behavior (#729). Until #1759 retired it, the canonical brief was janitor-prompt.md next to tools/baton-agy-loop/dispatch.py, passed via --prompt-file; baton dispatch janitor has no equivalent standing brief file today -- the operator supplies the checkers to run via --spec/--spec-text each time. The checkers determine the work, so the cheap tier runs it; anything needing judgment comes back [NOT DONE], not guessed at. #1355 kept network_access true here for the same reason as implement -- see implement's purpose field for the full reasoning (it is not agy-specific), not restated here.

outputs.name: janitor.md
outputs.instruction: Write a report of what you changed and which checkers are now green to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/janitor.md.

outputs.name: branch.diff
outputs.instruction: Write the full diff of the committed change to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/branch.diff -- this is the ground truth a following review reads, so it must be the diff of the change, not of HEAD.

purpose: Resident room occupant turn that reads room state and emits turn actions.

outputs.name: turn-actions.json
outputs.instruction: Write your turn actions JSON to $BATON_OUTPUT_DIR/turn-actions.json.
